packets.responsibility: THE single chokepoint every reader of a component's content resolves its internal frame through (CLAUDE.md §11's own citation). Branch precedence, in order: (1) an explicit per-outer-keyframe `componentFrame` override (2604-2612) — scans backward from `mainFrameIdx` to the nearest preceding outer keyframe (held span semantics identical to ordinary Animation 2D keys, not an exact-frame check) and, if that keyframe carries a `componentFrame` stamp, returns it directly (clamped into `[0,sym.totalFrames-1]`), bypassing every mode/speed/offset math below entirely; (2) Time Remap (`layer.timeRemap&&window.SMMotion&&SMMotion.timeRemapValue`, 2623-2626) — a keyframed curve (motion.js, C20, cited by name only) names the internal frame directly, overriding play mode/speed/placement wholesale, so freeze/hold/reverse/ramp all come from the curve; (3) `symPlayMode==='single'` — a frozen `symSingleFrame`, ignoring `mainFrameIdx` entirely; (4) `symPlayMode==='once'` — plays from `symTrimIn` (default 0) through `symTrimOut` (default `total-1`) and HOLDS at `symTrimOut` rather than rolling into unrelated symbol frames, the exact formula `enterMontageView`'s own synthetic montage segments rely on (app.js:4277-4335, general app.js territory, cited by name only); (5) `symPlayMode==='pingpong'` — bounces back and forth over a `(total-1)*2`-length cycle, returning `0` outright for a 1-frame symbol; (6) the default (`loop`) — a plain modulo of `elapsed` over `total`. `elapsed=max(0,mainFrameIdx-symPlacedAt)*symSpeed` is computed once up front and reused by every mode below the componentFrame/Time-Remap overrides.

future_proposals: nemo-script.js's own `Layer.prototype.unlinkTime` (line 340: `delete this._ld().timeLink; return this;`) bypasses `unlinkTimeLinkPreserveRange` entirely, unlike every UI-driven unlink gesture (layer-inout.js:1508, motion.js:7227/8379, timeline.js:6033/6584) — confirmed by direct read, no accompanying `ld.inPoint`/`ld.outPoint` write and no comment explaining the divergence, unlike the two OTHER bare-delete sites in the codebase (app.js:3957's merge-cleanup re-point, timeline.js:1251-1252's split-cut hard-value bake), both of which have their own explicit rationale. A script calling `unlinkTime()` on a linked layer therefore silently resets it to its full/auto range instead of preserving the range it visually had while linked — exactly the class of bug `unlinkTimeLinkPreserveRange`'s own header comment (2912-2917) was written to prevent for UI call sites. Not changed here (out of this census's read-only scope); a one-line fix would route `unlinkTime` through `window.unlinkTimeLinkPreserveRange` the same way layer-inout.js's own contextmenu handler already does.

Worth flagging explicitly for whoever next touches montage persistence or the export whitelist, since the absence looks identical to a missed field at a glance — see `boundaries` for the full trace. Not changed here.

`resolveLinkedTime`'s own offset read (`SMMotion.valueAtFrame(ld,offProp,state.currentFrame)`, line 2783) is explicitly `state.currentFrame`-scoped rather than frame-parametrized, per its own comment ("confirmed scope with Cyril"): an export pass that renders every frame without ever moving `state.currentFrame` would resolve a Parent-in-Time-linked layer's in/out with the SAME offset on every exported frame, even if the offset were ever keyframed in the future (it currently cannot be — motion.js's own `PROP_NO_STOPWATCH` hides the stopwatch on these two properties). Currently harmless (the offset is static in practice), but a plausible correctness gap the moment true per-frame time-link keyframing is considered — flagged here since this scope is the one place the design tradeoff is visible in code, not changed.
